JBU/nypd-stars.note: N531JL's fin stars traced from Commons 'JetBlue Airways A320-232, N531JL, named Blue Finest ... (2019-11-29)' (CC BY 2.0): 24 equal white stars, a loose ring with more inside.

ACA/roundel.note: The Air Canada roundel (2017): an open red ring whose foot runs into the maple leaf's stem, round an eleven-point leaf. Redrawn from Commons File:Air Canada logo.svg (PD-textlogo), simplified; the ring is the unit box, the stem's curl dips just below it.

AJT/star-a.note: Amerijet's star-A as a letter: a star in the first colour, the A's stroke (apex down to the lower right point) in the second, edged in white.

ANZ/koru.note: Air New Zealand's koru: an upper curl turning aft into a spiral, a lower curl mirroring it below, joined at a forward point, with two parallel bars running aft from the point to the trailing edge (carried past it, so the fin cuts them). Traced in outline from a photo of ZK-NZN; mirrored on the right, as on the aircraft (ZK-NZG).

COA/wordmark.note: Continental's 1950s fin wordmark (condensed slanted bold, tall C) as on N75435's retro: traced from Commons File:United Boeing 737-900ER N75435 Continental retro BWI MD3.jpg (2025-08-28, left side, the fin's lettering levelled). Baseline y 0, the C's cap height y 1; its slant is its own.

DLH/crane-disc.note: Pre-2018 Lufthansa tail (DLH/standard-1988, GEC/standard-1988): a yellow disc (slot 0) with a thin blue ring inset and the blue crane (slot 1). The crane and ring are DLH/crane-ring's (the 2018 refresh kept Otl Aicher's crane), set at 0.885 of the disc so the yellow shows round the ring, as on D-ABYK's fin (Commons, 2025-06-21: ring about 0.89 of the disc's width). Replaces a crane with both wings raised in a symmetric V, which read as a Y. Faces forward on both sides.

FIN/f.note: Finnair's ribbon F: redrawn from Commons File:Finnair F emblem.svg (PD-textlogo), simplified, its straight foot bar shortened from the emblem's 4.25 wide to the fin mark's 2.1975 so it sits where it did. Bottom of the foot bar y 0, top of the top arm y 1.

FIN/wordmark.note: Finnair's wordmark (heavy oblique capitals, rounded corners, the swept tops of the F, A and R): redrawn from Commons File:Finnair Logo.svg (PD-textlogo), simplified. Baseline y 0, cap height y 1.

JAL/tsurumaru.note: The tsurumaru (2011): a red egg of the crane's raised wings, three white feather slits curving down each lower side, a white oval above with the crane's S-shaped neck, round head and long beak in red facing forward (left); 'JAL' in white bold italic capitals across the foot. Our own drawing, measured from the CC0 photo of JA06XJ (Commons); not mirrored (the crane faces aft on the right, as on the aircraft).

JBU/dunkin-d.note: Dunkin's big rounded 'D' on the cup, measured off N643JB's left side (2026-09-11, Commons): tilted with the cup (about 15 degrees), its counter a D with two sharp corners at the stem. Lettering: kept readable on the right side, its tilt mirrored with the cup's (keep -15).

LOT/crane.note: LOT's crane in its ring (Tadeusz Gronowski, 1929): traced off Commons File:Embraer_ERJ-190-100_ERJ-190STD_(cn_487,_SP-LMG)_2023-03-17_Andre_Gerwing_Collection_ID_007541.jpg (left side), the photo's squash taken out by fitting the ring to a circle. Two broad round-ended wing strokes, the upper from high forward and the lower from low forward, meeting on the body; the body a wedge, round at the front, running to a point aft past the wings; a thin neck forward to a small head and beak. Faces forward on both sides.

QFA/kangaroo.note: The 2016 flying kangaroo as on the fin: leaping forward, head and pointed ear low toward the leading edge, a foreleg reaching up, the hind leg bent down to the root, the long tail sweeping up and aft to the trailing edge near the tip (carried past it, so the fin's edge cuts it). Traced in outline by colour from a side photo of VH-ZNC; the fin's edges crop it as on the aircraft.

QTR/oryx.note: The Qatar Airways oryx: the head facing forward with its pale ear and cheek, two long horns sweeping back and up, the mane down the back with its slits. Traced in outline from the fin of A7-BEW (Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0), where the horns run off the trailing edge (cut straight here). The fin itself draws it as its own areas; this is for the engines.

ROU/leaf-disc.note: Rouge's tail (2017): a huge red disc, cropped by the fin, with a big white maple leaf (rounded sinuses) whose top point meets the disc's edge just under the white band, tilted a little forward. Our own leaf, the flag's eleven points.

UAL/wordmark-1960s.note: United's 1960s wordmark (swash U, wide serif lowercase) as on N475UA's Friend Ship retro: traced from Commons File:N475UA (55208911135).jpg (2026-04-03, right side, the fuselage title levelled), its counter in the e restored by hand. Baseline y 0, the U's cap height y 1.

UAL/wordmark-1960s-fin.note: The same wordmark at the fin's normal width (the fuselage title is an extended cut): each letter of UAL/wordmark-1960s narrowed onto the letter positions measured on the fin in Commons File:United Airlines (85th Anniversary Retro Livery), Airbus A320-232, N475UA.jpg (2015-08-01, left side).

VIR/signature.note: The Virgin signature: redrawn from Commons File:Virgin-logo.svg (PD-textlogo), turned 26 degrees to level it as before (the livery's rotationDeg tilts it back), simplified. Baseline of 'irgin' y 0, top of the V's ball y 1; the swash and the g's tail hang below 0.

VIR/wordmark.note: Virgin Atlantic's lower-case title (2018): thin monoline letters, single-storey a, stems cut on a slant. Redrawn from Commons File:Virgin Atlantic logo 2018.svg (PD-textlogo), the lettering only, simplified. Baseline y 0, the l's and t's tops y 1.

CO1934/meatball.note: Our own simplified drawing of Continental's 1968 'meatball' (Saul Bass): a disc cut by six lines that start close together at its left edge and fan out, curving apart and widening, to its right; the lines show the paint under it. Not traced from the artwork. Mirrored on the right side so the lines meet toward the nose on both sides, as the photos show it.

CO1934/us-flag.note: The US flag, canton forward on both sides (Pan Am's flag geometry, our own drawing).

ML1979/metrolink.note: Our own simplified drawing of Midway Airlines' 1983 Metrolink mark, as painted on the forward fuselage: a gray bar over a red one, the red turning down from its forward end in a long diagonal to a point below, and a gray stroke inside the angle beside the diagonal, so the red and gray read as an M. Not traced from the artwork. Mirrored on the right side, so the diagonal starts at the forward end on both sides, as photos show it.

ML1979/metrolink-fin.note: Our own simplified drawing of the same Metrolink mark as painted on the fin: heavier bars, sheared aft with the fin (the bars are parallelograms) and taller than the body's. Not traced from the artwork. Mirrored on the right side.

ML1979/sunset-disc.note: Our own simplified drawing of Midway Airlines' 1979 tail mark: an orange disc crossed by a broad navy chevron pointing forward, its upper arm shallow and its lower arm steep, with two thin orange lines running inside it, so the stripes read as an M. Not traced from the artwork. Mirrored on the right side, so it points forward on both, as photos show it (N1056T right side 1979, N1065T left side 1980).

ML1979/red-m.note: Our own simplified drawing of Midway Airlines' 1986 tail mark, white on the red fin: a short bar on top; under it a longer bar whose forward end turns down and aft in one long arm to a point; a small triangle tucked inside the angle, so the pieces read as an M. Not traced from the artwork. Mirrored on the right side, the arm forward on both, as photos show it (N700ML left side 1988, N705ML right side 1988).

AL1979/us-flag.note: The US flag, canton forward on both sides (Pan Am's flag geometry, our own drawing), as USAir carried it small ahead of the registration.

SCX/sun-2001.note: Sun Country's 2001-2018 sun, our own simple drawing: a bold S (reading the right way on both sides, so not mirrored) ringed by twelve wedge rays, broad ends out, all in color 0; navy on the orange fin, navy on the forward light-blue disc (the field is the scheme's paint), orange on the blue winglets. Checked on N821SY (2016, 2019).

DWI/parrot.note: Our own simple drawing of Arajet's parrot, not traced from the artwork: a parrot's head facing left (forward on the left side), a thick violet arc over it, a black eye, a violet crescent round the front of a lighter violet rounded-triangle cheek, and four tapered feathers fanning down and aft from behind the eye (cyan, yellow, orange, green), the green and orange reaching the bottom. Mirrored on the right side so it faces the nose there too, as the photos show. Colors: violet, cheek, eye, cyan, yellow, orange, green.

DWI/flag.note: The Dominican flag simplified: blue and red quarters (blue top hoist, red bottom hoist) with a white cross; the coat of arms left out at this size. Colors: blue, red, white.

BWA/hummingbird.note: Our own drawing of Caribbean Airlines' 2020 tail art, by eye from 9Y-CAL (Commons, 2026-02-18, left side), not traced: a fan of long tapering feather streaks rising toward the fin's tip by its trailing edge (a broad red one at the heart, mauve and pink ones either side, thin yellow, lime and sky-blue streaks between them) and a band of short slanted streaks along the fin's foot, running forward over the fillet. Colors index the logo's colors: red, mauve, pink, magenta, orange, yellow, lime, sky. Mirrored on the right side so the feathers rise toward the trailing edge on both sides, as 9Y-ANT shows.

BWA/hummingbird-ribbons.note: Our own drawing of the ATR 72-600s' ribbon hummingbird along the windows, by eye from 9Y-TTJ (Commons, 2023-07-02, left side), not traced: a bundle of thin rainbow ribbons that waves along the window line, tight at the bird's head and fanning out at its tail aft, with a small looped head and a long thin beak forward. Lines drawn a little bolder than painted so they show at card size. Colors index the logo's colors: red, orange, mauve, magenta, yellow, lime, sky. Mirrored so the bird flies toward the nose on both sides.

SAM/presidential-seal.note: Our own simple mark for the Seal of the President of the United States as the VC-25As carry it beside the forward door: a gold rim, a dark blue ring (its lettering left out), a thin gold ring, and inside on dark blue a ring of thirteen white stars round a plain shield (a blue chief over red and white pales). The eagle, its arrows and olive branch, the scroll and the lettering are left out on purpose: at the sizes an app draws it (about 1.2 m on the jet) they'd be noise, and the seal's use is restricted by law (18 U.S.C. 713, Executive Order 11649), so a simplified roundel that reads as 'the seal' without copying it is the safer choice. A plainer fallback: the first four shapes only (gold rim, blue ring, gold ring, blue field). Colors: 0 sealGold, 1 sealNavy, 2 flagWhite, 3 flagRed, 4 flagBlue.

SAM/star-and-bar.note: The national insignia in full color, the same drawing as UCG/star-and-bar (a white star on a blue disc, white bars with a red stripe, outlined in blue). Colors: 0 insigniaBlue, 1 flagWhite, 2 insigniaRed.

AJT/star-flag.note: Amerijet's fin logo: a white-outlined star whose upper arms form an 'A' (a red stroke inside its navy outline), a white star's foot below, and red, navy and red bars edged in white running aft from it to the trailing edge. Colours: 0 the fin's navy (not drawn: it shows through), 1 white, 2 red. Traced by colour from a photo of N269CM.

QFA/roundel.note: Qantas' nose roundel: a red ring on white with the flying kangaroo inside it in red (our kangaroo, whole, scaled to sit inside the ring).

POE/wordmark-pattern.note: Porter's fin: the word 'porter' repeated in rows rising toward the trailing edge at about 30°, alternate rows white (0) and light blue (1) on the navy fin. Our own plain geometric lower case, not Porter's typeface; one tile, repeated across the fin, which clips it. Not mirrored: the words read on both sides.

ANZ/fern.note: The silver-fern frond on the black rear fuselage: its stem curving from low and forward up and aft toward the fin, tall leaflets above it, drooping leaflets below. Traced in outline from a photo of ZK-NZN (787-9) with the cabin windows, the aft door's outline and the registration taken out; mirrored on the right.

AFR/seahorse.note: Our own simple drawing of Air France's winged seahorse (hippocampe ailé) in its roundel, by eye from F-GSQL (Commons, New York JFK, 2026-10-05, left side), not traced: a thin ring; inside it a horse's head in profile facing forward, ears up and a tuft of mane behind them, an eye, a curving neck and body ending in a fish tail curled up at the back, a foreleg, and a wing of a leading stroke and three arcs fanning up to the right. Colors: navy, white (the disc). Not mirrored (not checked on a right-side photo).

KAL/kr-flag.note: The Taegukgi from its official construction (Commons' PD Flag_of_South_Korea.svg as the spec): white field, the red-over-blue taeguk turned along the diagonal, the four black trigrams (geon, gam, gon, ri). Colors: white, red, blue, black. Mirrored on the right side so its hoist is forward, as flags on aircraft are.

AAR/kr-flag.note: The Taegukgi, as KAL/kr-flag. Colors: white, red, blue, black. Mirrored on the right side so its hoist is forward.

CLX/luxembourg-flag.note: Luxembourg's flag, 5:3: red, white and light blue bands. Colors: red, white, blue.

LAE/colombia-flag.note: Colombia's flag, 3:2: yellow over the top half, blue and red quarters under it. Colors: yellow, blue, red.

AVA/flag.note: The aircraft's home flag, drawn as Colombia's (most of the fleet): yellow half, blue and red quarters, 3:2. Colors: yellow, blue, red.

ICE/flag.note: Iceland's flag, 25:18: blue field, a white Nordic cross 4 wide and a red cross 2 wide in it, the upright at 7-11 from the hoist. Colors: blue, white, red. Mirrored on the right side so its hoist is forward.

AFR/eu-flag.note: The European flag's ring of twelve upright gold stars, without its blue field (Air France puts it on the fin's navy stripe). Ring and star sizes from the flag's construction (ring radius a third of the flag's height, stars an eighteenth). Colors: gold.

GXA/brush-x.note: Our own simple drawing of GlobalX's brushed X (2022 scheme), by eye from N530FL (Commons, El Paso 2026-02-04), not traced: two broad strokes, the one rising to the right ending in a ragged brush tip at the top, the other running down to the right. On the fin it runs off the leading edge. Not mirrored: N570TA's right side (Commons, 2025-03-13, from below) shows the fuselage's X with its brush tip up and forward, the same picture as the left; the fin's right side wasn't seen. Color: blue.

GXA/wordmark.note: Our own drawing of GlobalX's GLOBAL lettering, by eye from N530FL: thin geometric capitals, the G a ring open at the upper right with a bar across its middle running out past it on the left, an A without a crossbar, a long foot on the first L. The brushed X after it is its own logo (GXA/brush-x). Box: baseline to cap height. Color: blue.

GXA/brush-x-fin.note: GXA/brush-x as painted on the fin, mirrored on the right side so the brush tip stays under the tip toward the trailing edge rather than running off the leading edge (the fin's right side wasn't seen on a photo; GlobalX's fuselage X is the same picture on both sides).

KLM/logo.note: KLM's logo as on its cowlings and winglets: the crown (KLM/crown) over our own KLM lettering (heavy rounded-free sans capitals, an M with its V reaching most of the way down), not traced. Color: one (blue).

UAE/calligraphy.note: Our own simplified drawing of the Emirates calligraphy (its name in Arabic), drawn by eye after the PD-textlogo file on Commons (File:Emirates_logo.svg), not traced: the two tall strokes, the looped lam-alef, the bar with the meem's head, the two diamond dots and the bowls. Script, so never mirrored.

VIR/flying-lady.note: Our own simple drawing of Virgin Atlantic's 2019 flying lady, by eye from G-VLUX (Commons, 2026-09-12, left side), not traced: a woman leaping toward the nose, one arm raised forward, the other holding a big Union flag that waves aft of her. Dark hair, a white top, red skirt and legs, a natural skin tone; drawn plainly, no caricature. The flag from its construction (saltires and cross), its red saltire not counterchanged at this size. Colors: red, navy, white. Mirrored on the right side so she leaps forward there too.

ITY/tricolor-flash.note: ITA's tricolor flash on the engines, under the name Open Liveries uses (liveries/ITY/standard.json: 'ITY/tricolor-flash'; the old ITY/tricolour-flash never matched, so the engines were blank). Traced off EI-HLE's left engine (Commons File:ITA_Airways_A220-100_EI-HLE_2024-06-15_Munich_Airport_p02.jpg): a green stroke leaning aft as it rises, a shorter red parallelogram below and behind it, both on the same slant (the old shape leaned forward with the red ahead). Slot 0 green, slot 1 red.

VKG/wordmark.note: Sunclass's title: 'SUNCLASS' in geometric capitals drawn inline (each stroke two thin parallel lines), with two small waves after the last S at cap height. Drawn as centerlines offset both ways, measured off Commons File:Sunclass_Airlines,_OY-TCF,_Airbus_A321-211_(52887015141).jpg (2023-05-09): cap height 42 px, the word 7.6 caps long, the waves 0.9 caps wide 0.17 behind it. Reads normally on both sides (the waves aft on the left, forward on the right, as photographed). Baseline y 0, cap height y 1.

UAL/globe-2010.note: Continental's globe as United kept it in 2010 (UAL/standard-2010): UAL/globe's own geometry, its disc gold (slot 0), its bars blue (slot 1) and its outer ring white (slot 2). The 2010 globe's thin white latitude rings are drawn as the gold gaps between the bars, as on UAL/globe: at a tail's size they read the same. Checked on N79521 (Commons, 2023-04-16).

ETH/tricolor.note: The same shape as ETH/tricolour under the name Open Liveries uses (liveries/ETH/*.json logos: 'ETH/tricolor'); the British spelling never matched, so it wasn't drawn.

JBU/fdny-panel.note: FDNY tail panel art on N615JB: 'FIRE DEPARTMENT' arched in gold, 'CITY OF / NEW YORK' in white, the skyline with the twin towers. Lettering set in Arial Bold to the photos' layout; the same picture on both sides, as painted.

JBU/fdny-cross.note: FDNY's Maltese cross on N615JB's aft fuselage, in the badge's white field: white arms outlined in blue with blue ladder rungs, a red ring, red center (the hydrant and lettering left out).

AAL/aa-eagle-roundel.note: American's 1930s roundel as on the Flagship 777 (N735AT): navy disc, white rim, red AA either side of a white eagle. Built from AAL/aa-eagle.

SWA/nevada-sagebrush.note: Nevada One's sagebrush: two sprays of green leaves with yellow flower clusters, an open wreath under the star (simplified, from Commons photos of N8646B).
